discovery: Photonic bandgap materials and photonic crystal fibres for controlling light with wavelength-scale structure

nominees.name: Philip St. J. Russell
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, Erlangen, Germany

motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently predicted that periodic dielectric structures can open a photonic bandgap. In such a structure the propagation of light, and even spontaneous emission, is forbidden, and photons can be localized. Yablonovitch then demonstrated the first three-dimensional bandgap material. Russell turned the concept into photonic crystal fibre, a glass fibre with wavelength-scale holes, including hollow-core fibre that guides light by a bandgap in air. This gave engineered dispersion, endlessly single-mode guidance, supercontinuum white-light sources and gas-filled fibre nonlinear optics. Together these works established that light can be confined and controlled by structuring matter at the scale of its wavelength. That principle underlies modern nanophotonics: photonic crystal cavities and lasers, slow light, topological photonics, low-latency hollow-core communication links, and ultrafast and quantum light sources. They began as a fundamental physical idea and became global experimental platforms.
